videos.script: DeepEval and RAGAS do what the last four lessons did by hand, inside a structure: a test case, a metric, a runner. {{structure}} Before the first run, three things. Both send telemetry unless told not to. DeepEval keeps every test case on disk. And RAGAS needed three packages pinned before it would import. {{install}} Most of their metrics are prompts to a model. Pointed at the lab's judge, one is refused, and the log shows what it asked. {{asks}} Without a model, the structure still works. The course's own checks run inside DeepEval and give the same counts. {{own}} RAGAS has metrics that need no model. Its context precision agrees with ours. Its recall does not, because it counts chunks where ours counts sections. {{recall}} Read a metric before you run it, and measure it before you trust it. {{end}}
